newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turkish navy ships arrive in north Cyprus.
newsitem.headline: Turkish navy ships arrive in north Cyprus.

text.p: Three Turkish navy ships docked at a northern Cypriot port on Saturday in a show of strength amid a row over the deployment of surface-to-air missiles on the divided eastern Mediterranean island.
Witnesses said around 5,000 Turkish Cypriots welcomed the frigate "Fatih" and the assault boats "Gurbet" and "Dogan" when they cruised into Famagusta harbour.
The visit was part of a show of solidarity by Turkey with its ethnic kin in Cyprus against Greek Cypriot plans to install Russian-made S-300 missiles on the island.
Turkey has said it would use force to halt the deployment, due in around 16 months.

"You did not come here to threaten people with war, you came here to bring to the path of common sense those people who are threatening war," Turkish Cypriot Taner Etkin said in a speech on the quayside.
Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 in response to a coup in Nicosia that was backed by Athens. A breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in the north of Cyprus is recognised only by Ankara.
